source.title: Generalization in Graph Neural Networks: Improved PAC-Bayesian Bounds on Graph Diffusion
source.authors: Hao-Tian Ju; Dong-Yue Li; Aneesh Sharma; Hongyang Zhang

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Measures Hessian-based noise stability against observed training–test gaps and tests noise-stability optimization, using a different measure and intervention from the claim versions.
record.gate_note: Figure 1b's numerical values and Figure 3's plotted values are not recoverable from the supplied text; captions and prose describe their direction. Table 2 compares test ROC-AUC across regularization methods, but gives no no-dropout reference or training–test gap, so it does not test V6 or a versioned claim.
record.test_reason: The study measures Hessian-based bounds and noise-stability optimization in GNNs, which fit none of V1–V8. Its closest connection is V7, but it does not measure tolerance to magnitude-scaled weight perturbations or compare rankings of generalization gaps against norm- and margin-based measures. V1 is cited as background.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's empirical paraphrase is accurate. The authors also conclude that their PAC-Bayesian bounds improve dependence on graph structure from maximum degree to diffusion-matrix spectral norm, with a matching asymptotic lower-bound construction. They report qualitative agreement between Hessian-based bounds and observed gaps, and improved test ROC-AUC from noise-stability optimization across five molecular graph datasets.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes graph neural networks and uses Hessian-based noise stability and perturbed-weight fine-tuning; the listed claim versions concern other architectures, interventions, or a magnitude-aware sharpness measure.
record.method_sensitivity: Training-set size: the authors say noise-stability optimization reduces the generalization gap particularly when BACE training-set size is N = 600.

fits_no_version.finding: The Hessian-based generalization bound qualitatively matches the scale of observed GNN loss gaps across depths.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hessian-based noise-stability bounds can track the scale of generalization gaps in graph neural networks.

fits_no_version.finding: On BACE, noise-stability optimization reduces training–test loss gaps relative to early stopping, particularly with 600 training examples, and reduces Hessian trace and largest eigenvalue.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizing perturbed-weight losses can reduce generalization gaps and Hessian curvature during pretrained GNN fine-tuning.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS), 2023
record.problems: The generalization-gap and Hessian comparisons in Figures 1 and 3 are described qualitatively, with plotted values unavailable in the supplied text. The BACE comparison uses early stopping, and the reported performance table gives test ROC-AUC rather than training–test gaps.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 test ROC-AUC comparisons among regularization methods were omitted because they do not report training–test gaps or a comparable no-dropout condition. Figure 3's perturbation-count and negated-perturbation ablations were omitted because they evaluate the proposed method rather than a mapped claim version.

untested.parts: Own experiments comparing random-label fitting and held-out performance with natural-label generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer performance under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects in fully connected or convolutional classifiers under comparable dropout and no-dropout conditions. Table 2 compares regularization methods for pretrained GIN fine-tuning.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, its association with gaps among comparably fitted convolutional networks, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: States marked cannot_determine concern the named claim versions, not whether the paper reports its own qualitative effects. Figure-only numerical values are unnecessary to establish the explicitly stated directions. No verdict labels apply because no version is tested.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error across widths beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizers and their tuning.
Large versus small batch training and adaptations to the recipe.
Dropout effects relative to a comparable no-dropout condition.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbation sharpness and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.
